title: Thermodynamics of Ahn--Doherty--Landahl Continuous Quantum Error Correction
authors: Juan Garcia-Nila, Pedro B. Melo, Lucas Johns
abstract: Continuous quantum error correction (CQEC) replaces discrete syndrome measurements and recovery operations with continuous syndrome extraction and real-time Hamiltonian feedback. Here we investigate the thermodynamic resources required by this process by formulating measurement-based continuous quantum error correction as an information engine. We distinguish the system-side power associated with energy transfer between the feedback field and the protected system from the controller-side power associated with the feedback Hamiltonian. The framework is first developed for the one-qubit Ahn-Doherty-Landahl (ADL) protocol and subsequently extended to the three-qubit repetition code under continuous stabilizer monitoring. Numerical simulations show that increasing the feedback strength improves the steady-state fidelity and reduces the conditional-state entropy, while both energetic contributions continue to increase in magnitude after the fidelity begins to saturate. These results expose a direct tradeoff between logical stabilization and the energetic resources required for continuous feedback, closely related to previously established energy--precision tradeoffs in quantum measurement and quantum-Zeno stabilization.
summary: This work develops a thermodynamic framework to quantify the energy costs associated with Continuous Quantum Error Correction (CQEC). By treating the process as an information engine, the authors show that achieving higher logical fidelity necessitates an ever-increasing expenditure of energy from the feedback mechanism. This establishes a fundamental energy-precision trade-off for quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the thermodynamic resources (energy, work, entropy) required by Continuous Quantum Error Correction (CQEC) protocols.
main_result: It establishes a direct, quantifiable trade-off: improving logical fidelity requires a continuously increasing energetic investment from the feedback controller, even after fidelity saturates.
method: The analysis formulates CQEC as a non-equilibrium information engine, applying the first law of thermodynamics to the system's evolution governed by a stochastic master equation.
model_or_system: The study models CQEC using the one-qubit Ahn-Doherty-Landahl (ADL) protocol and extends it to the three-qubit repetition code. The dynamics are described by a stochastic master equation incorporating system Hamiltonian evolution, noise, and continuous feedback.
key_observables: Logical Fidelity ($F$), Internal Energy ($U$), System-side Power ($P_{sys}$), Feedback Power ($P_{fb}$), and Conditional-State Entropy ($S(ho_c)$).
important_parameters: Feedback strength ($\Omega$), Noise rate ($\gamma$), Monitoring strength ($\kappa$), and system Hamiltonian parameters ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between system-side energy transfer and controller-side work, treating the process as a genuine non-equilibrium thermodynamic process.
figures_summary: Figures summarize the evolution of logical codespace fidelity, asymptotic average system and feedback power costs, and the relationship between power cost and logical fidelity.
paper_structure: The paper develops the thermodynamic framework for CQEC, first on a minimal one-qubit system, deriving the first law decomposition. It then extends this analysis to the three-qubit repetition code, demonstrating the energetic cost scaling with increasing feedback strength.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous thermodynamic cost accounting for quantum control, linking fundamental concepts like energy dissipation and information processing limits to practical quantum error correction schemes.
